result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A is a clean table sorted with the most overdue first. Its 'Overdue N days' labels make status clear in words, and amounts sit in one column aligned on the decimal point under a ($) header. It also splits the part-paid invoice into Total, Received and Balance due. B also sorts and labels status well and shows the part-paid balance, but it uses cards: dates are folded into text lines rather than their own columns, amounts repeat the $ on every row, and the list runs below the fold, so it is harder to scan at a glance. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B uses a proper table, with right-aligned amounts in separate Total, Received and Balance columns, the currency stated in the headers, and dates in their own column. Overdue rows get text labels and are sorted most overdue first. A sorts and labels well, and it shows the part-paid balance clearly. But A's card layout puts dates inline with other text and spreads amounts across cards, so they don't line up as a column, and the page runs past one screen.
